applicability: Onboarding and periodic review of vendors, agents, consultants, and intermediaries
notes: Screening control; not a legal or fraud determination.
recommended_action: Pause automated approval; obtain or refresh diligence and document the rationale for the risk tier.
source_title: Evaluation of Corporate Compliance Programs
text: Match diligence depth to third-party risk. Applicability: Onboarding and periodic review of vendors, agents, consultants, and intermediaries. Review condition: Escalate when risk-based diligence is absent, stale, or materially weaker than the third party's risk profile. Recommended reviewer action: Pause automated approval; obtain or refresh diligence and document the rationale for the risk tier. Evidence to preserve: vendor_risk_rating, diligence_completed_at, jurisdictions, services, ownership, qualifications, reputation. Caveat: Screening control; not a legal or fraud determination.

applicability: Vendor or intermediary engagement and invoice approval
notes: Part of a broader risk-based program.
recommended_action: Request business-owner attestation and supporting scope documents before payment.
source_title: Evaluation of Corporate Compliance Programs
text: Document the business rationale for using the third party. Applicability: Vendor or intermediary engagement and invoice approval. Review condition: Escalate when no documented business need connects the third party, its services, and the transaction. Recommended reviewer action: Request business-owner attestation and supporting scope documents before payment. Evidence to preserve: business_owner, business_rationale, statement_of_work, invoice_description, purchase_order_id. Caveat: Part of a broader risk-based program.

applicability: Invoices and payments to third parties
notes: Compensation reasonableness is contextual; do not use a universal threshold.
recommended_action: Perform scope-to-invoice and market-rate review; route unexplained variances for human approval.
source_title: Evaluation of Corporate Compliance Programs
text: Verify services and compensation are reasonable. Applicability: Invoices and payments to third parties. Review condition: Escalate when the contract does not clearly describe the services, evidence of work is missing, or compensation appears inconsistent with the industry and geography. Recommended reviewer action: Perform scope-to-invoice and market-rate review; route unexplained variances for human approval. Evidence to preserve: contract_scope, invoice_description, deliverable_evidence, amount, currency, market_benchmark, country. Caveat: Compensation reasonableness is contextual; do not use a universal threshold.

applicability: Active vendors and intermediaries
notes: Cadence should be risk-based.
recommended_action: Refresh controls based on risk and document completion or an approved exception.
source_title: Evaluation of Corporate Compliance Programs
text: Continue monitoring after onboarding. Applicability: Active vendors and intermediaries. Review condition: Escalate when a relationship lacks refreshed diligence, training, audits, certifications, or risk-based monitoring during its lifecycle. Recommended reviewer action: Refresh controls based on risk and document completion or an approved exception. Evidence to preserve: last_diligence_date, last_training_date, certification_status, audit_status, contract_end_date, risk_rating. Caveat: Cadence should be risk-based.

applicability: Vendor master creation and reactivation
notes: Use privacy-preserving entity matching.
recommended_action: Block automated onboarding and require compliance review with entity-resolution evidence.
source_title: Evaluation of Corporate Compliance Programs
text: Prevent re-engagement of rejected or terminated third parties. Applicability: Vendor master creation and reactivation. Review condition: Escalate when a prospective vendor matches a previously rejected, suspended, or terminated entity or its related parties. Recommended reviewer action: Block automated onboarding and require compliance review with entity-resolution evidence. Evidence to preserve: vendor_name, owners, addresses, bank_account_token, tax_identifier_token, prior_disposition, termination_reason. Caveat: Use privacy-preserving entity matching.

applicability: US federal proposal analysis and analogous internal price review
notes: Applicability outside federal acquisition requires local policy mapping.
recommended_action: Select and document one or more suitable comparison techniques before approval.
source_title: FAR 15.404-1 Proposal analysis
text: Ground price reasonableness in comparable evidence. Applicability: US federal proposal analysis and analogous internal price review. Review condition: Escalate when price approval lacks comparison to competition, prior prices adjusted for differences, parametric estimates, market prices, independent estimates, or market research. Recommended reviewer action: Select and document one or more suitable comparison techniques before approval. Evidence to preserve: proposed_price, competitive_quotes, historical_prices, quantity, terms, market_index, independent_estimate, market_research. Caveat: Applicability outside federal acquisition requires local policy mapping.

applicability: Offers with multiple priced line items
notes: Requires contextual price analysis.
recommended_action: Assess performance and payment risk and document whether the imbalance creates unacceptable risk.
source_title: FAR 15.404-1 Proposal analysis
text: Detect materially unbalanced line-item pricing. Applicability: Offers with multiple priced line items. Review condition: Flag line items priced materially above or below reasonable cost or price relationships even when the total offer appears acceptable. Recommended reviewer action: Assess performance and payment risk and document whether the imbalance creates unacceptable risk. Evidence to preserve: line_item_prices, quantities, cost_estimates, market_prices, total_offer, delivery_schedule. Caveat: Requires contextual price analysis.

applicability: Customers, suppliers, intermediaries, counterparties, products, services, and geographies
notes: Legal applicability and list status must be checked at decision time.
recommended_action: Apply documented risk assessment and route high-risk cases to the sanctions team.
source_title: A Framework for OFAC Compliance Commitments
text: Assess sanctions risk across parties and transactions. Applicability: Customers, suppliers, intermediaries, counterparties, products, services, and geographies. Review condition: Escalate when a covered relationship or transaction has not been assessed against its sanctions exposure. Recommended reviewer action: Apply documented risk assessment and route high-risk cases to the sanctions team. Evidence to preserve: customer_country, vendor_country, beneficiary_country, intermediaries, products, services, shipping_route, risk_rating. Caveat: Legal applicability and list status must be checked at decision time.

applicability: New customer and vendor onboarding
notes: Use current official sanctions lists and qualified reviewers.
recommended_action: Complete risk rating and enhanced review when warranted before enabling transactions.
source_title: A Framework for OFAC Compliance Commitments
text: Risk-rate parties during onboarding. Applicability: New customer and vendor onboarding. Review condition: Escalate when onboarding lacks a documented sanctions risk rating based on submitted information and appropriate independent research. Recommended reviewer action: Complete risk rating and enhanced review when warranted before enabling transactions. Evidence to preserve: legal_name, aliases, ownership, addresses, countries, industry, independent_research, risk_rating. Caveat: Use current official sanctions lists and qualified reviewers.

applicability: Party and transaction screening systems
notes: A model score must not replace required legal screening.
recommended_action: Update lists and matching logic; retest before clearing affected alerts.
source_section: Internal Controls; Root Causes of Compliance Breakdowns
source_title: A Framework for OFAC Compliance Commitments
text: Keep screening logic and identifiers current. Applicability: Party and transaction screening systems. Review condition: Escalate when screening lists, identifier coverage, transliteration, alternate spellings, or system calibration are stale or incomplete. Recommended reviewer action: Update lists and matching logic; retest before clearing affected alerts. Evidence to preserve: screening_list_version, list_updated_at, name_variants, identifiers, calibration_test_at, false_negative_tests. Caveat: A model score must not replace required legal screening.

applicability: Potential sanctions matches and prohibited transactions
notes: Human and legal review required.
recommended_action: Hold the transaction and follow the organization's approved sanctions procedure.
source_title: A Framework for OFAC Compliance Commitments
text: Identify, interdict, escalate, report, and preserve records. Applicability: Potential sanctions matches and prohibited transactions. Review condition: Escalate when a potential match can proceed without a documented path to stop or reject the transaction, investigate, report when required, and retain evidence. Recommended reviewer action: Hold the transaction and follow the organization's approved sanctions procedure. Evidence to preserve: screening_alert_id, transaction_status, case_owner, decision, reporting_status, record_retention_until. Caveat: Human and legal review required.

applicability: Corporate Transparency Act reporting scope for domestic entities, U.S. persons, and qualifying foreign reporting companies.
notes: Review evidence only; not proof of fraud or a legal determination.
recommended_action: Determine entity type and applicable exemption before treating BOI status as a control gap; independently collect ownership evidence when required by another control.
source_title: Beneficial Ownership Information Reporting
text: FinCEN's final rule effective August 14, 2026 exempts U.S.-created companies and U.S. persons from Corporate Transparency Act BOI reporting. Qualifying foreign entities registered to do business in a U.S. jurisdiction generally remain reporting companies, subject to exemptions, and do not report U.S.-person beneficial owners. Do not treat a missing FinCEN BOI filing by a domestic company as suspicious by itself; obtain ownership evidence directly when another compliance, contract, sanctions, tax, or procurement control requires it.

applicability: Banks, broker-dealers, mutual funds, futures commission merchants, and introducing brokers covered by the BSA CDD rule.
notes: Review evidence only; not proof of fraud or a legal determination.
recommended_action: Confirm covered-institution status and retain the ownership-verification and monitoring evidence used for the relationship.
source_title: FinCEN Reminds Financial Institutions that the CDD Rule Becomes Effective Today
text: FinCEN's Customer Due Diligence rule requires covered financial institutions to identify and verify customers and beneficial owners of legal-entity customers, understand the nature and purpose of relationships to develop risk profiles, and conduct ongoing monitoring. The rule applies to specified covered financial institutions, not automatically to every commercial payer; vendor-review systems should record why the rule applies before relying on it.

applicability: Federal agencies, personnel, and Government-contractor relationships; private-company policies may be broader.
notes: Review evidence only; not proof of fraud or a legal determination.
recommended_action: Route disclosed or detected relationships and benefits to the designated ethics or contracting reviewer; do not infer intent from a relationship alone.
source_title: FAR Part 3 — Improper Business Practices and Personal Conflicts of Interest
text: FAR 3.101 requires federal business to be conducted impartially and directs avoidance of actual conflicts of interest and their appearance in Government-contractor relationships. Government employees generally may not solicit or accept gifts, favors, entertainment, loans, or other things of value from parties seeking or conducting agency business, subject to authorized exceptions.

applicability: Federal contracts containing the clause, subject to the clause prescription and stated exceptions.
notes: Review evidence only; not proof of fraud or a legal determination.
recommended_action: Preserve evidence, confirm clause applicability, and route credible-evidence determinations to qualified legal and contracting personnel.
source_title: FAR 52.203-13 Contractor Code of Business Ethics and Conduct
text: When FAR 52.203-13 is included and its requirements apply, contractors must exercise due diligence to prevent and detect criminal conduct, maintain specified ethics and internal-control measures, and timely disclose credible evidence of covered fraud, conflict-of-interest, bribery, gratuity, or False Claims Act violations to the agency OIG and contracting officer. Applicability and clause exceptions must be checked against the actual contract.

applicability: Commercial products and commercial services contracts containing FAR 52.212-4.
notes: Review evidence only; not proof of fraud or a legal determination.
recommended_action: Perform an invoice-to-contract and acceptance match; return incomplete invoices through the authorized process rather than treating incompleteness alone as fraud.
source_title: FAR 52.212-4 Contract Terms and Conditions—Commercial Products and Commercial Services
text: For commercial products and services contracts using FAR 52.212-4, an invoice includes contractor identity, invoice date and number, contract and line-item references, description, quantity, unit of measure, unit and extended prices, shipping information when applicable, discount terms, payment destination, a defective-invoice contact, and required tax or EFT information. Payment is for items accepted and delivered under the contract.

applicability: Commercial products and commercial services contracts containing FAR 52.212-4.
notes: Review evidence only; not proof of fraud or a legal determination.
recommended_action: Hold duplicate release where authorized, calculate the overpayment, preserve the match evidence, and follow the contract's remittance and notice process.
source_title: FAR 52.212-4 Contract Terms and Conditions—Commercial Products and Commercial Services
text: Under FAR 52.212-4(i)(5), a contractor that becomes aware of a duplicate invoice or contract-financing payment, or another Government overpayment, must remit the amount with a description and provide supporting documentation to the contracting officer. The duplicate or overpayment amount and the discovery, notice, remittance, and supporting-document dates should be preserved.

applicability: Federal invoice payments, subject to the exceptions and contract-specific payment terms in Subpart 32.9.
notes: Review evidence only; not proof of fraud or a legal determination.
recommended_action: Require a documented contract/receipt/invoice match before payment unless a documented regulatory or contract exception applies.
source_title: FAR Subpart 32.9 — Prompt Payment
text: FAR 32.905 states that federal payment is based on a proper invoice and satisfactory contract performance. Except for the stated interim-service-payment exception, an invoice payment must be supported by a receiving report or other Government documentation authorizing payment, with contract, delivery, acceptance, and quantity information.

applicability: Issuers covered by Exchange Act Section 13(b), including the statute's rules for controlled and minority-owned entities.
notes: Review evidence only; not proof of fraud or a legal determination.
recommended_action: Confirm issuer applicability and reconcile vendor-payment records to authorization, accounting, and asset evidence; escalate unexplained differences for human review.
source_title: Recordkeeping and Internal Controls Provisions — Securities Exchange Act Section 13(b)
text: Exchange Act Section 13(b) requires covered issuers to keep books, records, and accounts that accurately and fairly reflect transactions and asset dispositions in reasonable detail, and to maintain internal accounting controls providing reasonable assurance for authorization, recording, controlled asset access, and periodic comparison of recorded and existing assets. Applicability depends on issuer status and control relationships.

applicability: Records generated under contracts containing the audit clauses identified in FAR 4.702, subject to longer contract-specific periods and exceptions.
notes: Review evidence only; not proof of fraud or a legal determination.
recommended_action: Calculate retention from the applicable FAR and contract terms, preserve the longest applicable period, and maintain integrity evidence for electronic transfers.
source_title: FAR Subpart 4.7 — Contractor Records Retention
text: For contracts within FAR Subpart 4.7's scope, accounts-receivable invoices, purchase orders, paid checks, accounts-payable support, vendor invoices, invoice audits, receiving and inspection reports, purchase-order backup, and specified quality-control records generally have four-year retention periods. Computer-record transfers must preserve integrity, reliability, security, and an audit trail; contract-specific requirements may change the period.
